provenance.source: NCERT Mathematics Class 8, Chapter 1 'Rational Numbers' — rational numbers between two rational numbers, and representation on the number line. The misconceptions are the ones this topic reliably produces: carrying over the integer intuition that numbers have neighbours, and comparing negative fractions by size of digits.
provenance.note: m1 (thinking two fractions can be 'next to each other') is the deepest misconception in the whole chapter. It is not carelessness — it is a correct intuition about integers being applied where it does not hold, and a student who does not lose it will struggle with real numbers in Class 9.

topic.title: Rational Numbers Between Two Rational Numbers

concepts.title: Comparing rational numbers on the number line
concepts.statement: Number line pe jo number daayein (right) hota hai wo bada hota hai. Do rational numbers compare karne ke liye unka denominator ek jaisa banao, phir numerator dekho. Negative numbers me jiska 'size' bada hai wo chhota hota hai.
concepts.hook: Socho do doston ke paas paisa hai — ek pe ₹200 ka karza hai aur doosre pe ₹500 ka. Kaun behtar haalat me hai? Wo jispe kam karza hai, yaani $-200$. Number line pe $-200$, $-500$ ke daayein baithta hai. Ab sawal: $-\frac{2}{3}$ aur $-\frac{5}{6}$ me kaun bada hai?

analogies.text: Temperature: $-2°$ aur $-8°$ me $-2°$ zyada garam hai, chahe 8 bada number dikhta ho.
Lift ka basement: B2 aur B5 me B2 upar hai — zameen ke zyada kareeb.

formulas.note: Cross-multiply karke compare karo — par denominator dono positive hone chahiye.
Negative side pe bada dikhne wala number chhota hota hai.

misconceptions.wrong_belief: $-\frac{5}{6}$, $-\frac{2}{3}$ se bada hai kyunki 5 aur 6, 2 aur 3 se bade hain.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Negative side pe ulta chalta hai. $-\frac{5}{6}$ zero se zyada door hai, yaani zyada 'neeche' — isliye chhota hai. Karze wali baat yaad karo: zyada karza matlab buri haalat.
misconceptions.correction: Negative me jitna bada size, utna chhota number. $-\frac{5}{6} < -\frac{2}{3}$.
misconceptions.probe: $-2$ aur $-8$ me kaun bada hai? Ab wahi soch $-\frac{5}{6}$ aur $-\frac{2}{3}$ pe lagao.

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Do fractions compare karne ke liye numerator aur denominator alag-alag compare kar lo — $\frac{3}{7}$, $\frac{2}{5}$ se bada hai kyunki 3 > 2 aur 7 > 5.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Fraction ek hi number hai, do nahi. Upar-neeche alag compare karne ka koi matlab nahi — $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{3}{100}$ dekho: 3 > 1 hai, par $\frac{3}{100}$ bahut chhota hai.
misconceptions.correction: Denominator same banao, phir numerator dekho. Ya cross-multiply karo.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{3}{100}$ me kaun bada hai? Numerator dekhkar batao — kya wo tareeka kaam kiya?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{3}$ ke beech koi rational number nahi hai — ye 'aas-paas' wale numbers hain.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Integers me 2 aur 3 ke beech kuch nahi hota, par rational numbers me aisa nahi. Kisi bhi do rational numbers ke beech ANANT rational numbers hote hain. Beech wala nikalne ka aasan tareeka: dono ka average lo.
misconceptions.correction: Do rational numbers ke beech hamesha aur numbers hote hain — anant. Average lo, aur beech wala mil jaayega.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{3}$ ka average nikalo. Kya wo dono ke beech me aata hai?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Beech ka number nikalne ke liye numerator aur denominator ka alag-alag average le lo — $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{4}$ ke beech $\frac{1}{3}$ hai.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Ye sanyog se kabhi-kabhi kaam kar jaata hai aur usse bharosa ban jaata hai. Sahi tareeka poore numbers ka average hai: $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{4}$ ka average $\frac{3}{8}$ hai, $\frac{1}{3}$ nahi.
misconceptions.correction: Average matlab $\frac{a + b}{2}$ — poore numbers jodo, phir 2 se bhaag do.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{4}$ ko jodo aur 2 se bhaag do. Kya $\frac{1}{3}$ aaya?

steps: Ab dono ka denominator 6 hai: $-\frac{4}{6}$ aur $-\frac{5}{6}$
Negative side pe kam size wala bada hota hai, aur 4 < 5

worked_examples.problem: $\frac{1}{3}$ aur $\frac{1}{2}$ ke beech ek rational number nikalo.
steps: Check: $\frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{12}$, $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{6}{12}$, aur $\frac{5}{12}$ theek beech me hai

worked_examples.problem: $\frac{1}{4}$ aur $\frac{1}{2}$ ke beech teen rational numbers nikalo.
steps: Dono ko ek bade common denominator pe le jao: $\frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{8}$ aur $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$
Beech me sirf $\frac{3}{8}$ dikha — teen chahiye, to denominator aur bada karo
Ab beech me teen mil gaye: $\frac{5}{16}, \frac{6}{16}, \frac{7}{16}$

options.text: Negative numbers compare nahi kiye ja sakte

questions.solution: $-\frac{2}{3} = -\frac{4}{6}$. Ab $-\frac{4}{6}$ aur $-\frac{5}{6}$ — negative side pe kam size wala bada hota hai, to $-\frac{4}{6}$ bada hai. Number line pe wo daayein baithta hai.
$\frac{1}{2} = \frac{50}{100}$, jo $\frac{3}{100}$ se kaafi bada hai. Numerator alag se dekhna (3 > 1) yahan poori tarah galat jawab deta hai — fraction ek hi number hai.

questions.stem: $\frac{1}{3}$ aur $\frac{1}{2}$ ke beech kitne rational numbers hain?

options.text: Ek bhi nahi — ye aas-paas wale numbers hain

questions.solution: Kisi bhi do alag rational numbers ke beech anant rational numbers hote hain. Ek nikalne ke baad usse aur ek sire ke beech phir se average liya ja sakta hai, aur ye kabhi khatam nahi hota.

questions.stem: $\frac{1}{3}$ aur $\frac{1}{2}$ ka average nikalo. Jawab dashamlav me char sthaan tak likho.
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{6} + \frac{3}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. 2 se bhaag: $\frac{5}{12} \approx 0.4167$. Ye theek dono ke beech me hai.

questions.stem: Rohan kehta hai: '$\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{4}$ ke beech $\frac{1}{3}$ hai, kyunki 3, 2 aur 4 ke beech me hai.' Iske baare me kya sahi hai?

options.text: $\frac{1}{3}$ sach me beech me hai, par uska tareeka galat hai — average $\frac{3}{8}$ hai
Tareeka bhi sahi hai aur jawab bhi
Beech me koi number ho hi nahi sakta

questions.solution: $\frac{1}{4} = 0.25$, $\frac{1}{3} \approx 0.333$, $\frac{1}{2} = 0.5$ — to $\frac{1}{3}$ waqai beech me hai. Par Rohan ka tareeka sanyog se chala: sahi average $\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{3}{8}$ hai. Us tareeke pe bharosa mat karo — agli baar galat jawab dega.

questions.stem: In me se kaun-kaun se numbers $\frac{1}{4}$ aur $\frac{1}{2}$ ke BEECH me hain?
questions.solution: Sabko 16 ke denominator pe laao: $\frac{1}{4} = \frac{4}{16}$, $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{8}{16}$. Ab $\frac{3}{8} = \frac{6}{16}$ ✓ aur $\frac{5}{16}$ ✓ beech me hain. $\frac{1}{8} = \frac{2}{16}$ chhota hai aur $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{12}{16}$ bada.

questions.stem: $-\frac{1}{2}$ aur $-\frac{1}{3}$ ke beech wala number (average) nikalo. Jawab dashamlav me char sthaan tak.
questions.solution: $-\frac{1}{2} + \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = -\frac{3}{6} - \frac{2}{6} = -\frac{5}{6}$. 2 se bhaag: $-\frac{5}{12} \approx -0.4167$. Check: $-0.5 < -0.4167 < -0.333$ ✓ — negative side pe bhi average beech me hi aata hai.

questions.stem: Integers me 2 aur 3 ke beech koi integer nahi hota, par rational numbers me $\frac{1}{2}$ aur $\frac{1}{3}$ ke beech anant numbers hote hain. Samjhao aisa kyun hai.

rubric: Integers me har number ka ek 'agla' hota hai — 2 ke baad seedha 3
Rational numbers me aisa koi 'agla' hai hi nahi
Kisi bhi do rational numbers ka average nikalo — wo hamesha unke beech me aata hai aur khud rational hota hai
Ye kaam dobara kiya ja sakta hai, anant baar — isliye beech me anant numbers hain

questions.solution: Integers me har number ka ek turant agla hota hai: 2 ke baad 3, beech me kuch nahi. Rational numbers me aisa 'agla' hota hi nahi. Koi bhi do rational numbers $a$ aur $b$ lo — unka average $\frac{a+b}{2}$ hamesha unke beech me hoga, aur wo khud bhi rational hoga (do rational jodne aur 2 se bhaag dene par rational hi milta hai). Ab $a$ aur us naye number ke beech phir se average lo — phir ek naya mil gaya. Ye kabhi khatam nahi hota, isliye beech me anant rational numbers hain.
